answers.answer: For each held office card, roll one die and add one per fatigue on that card; Chairman also adds one. Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire. Move the member to Pensioners, flip the card to Vacant Offices, and return its fatigue to supply. Commanders have no office card and do not roll normal attrition.

Only players who retired at least one pensioner select or discard one display card. They act in descending actual total retirement spending; ties go to more total prize windows including new prizes, then clockwise from the PM. Acting player may peek at display blackmails. Do not replace cards during selection; if the display empties, skip remaining eligible players. Then discard all remaining display cards and refill exactly three (prestige faceup, blackmail facedown), even if nobody selected one. Return all unused Pensioners to supply.

At the start of your Family action, check whether the opportunity marker already matched the main action you choose. Take that main action once, or twice if it already matched; then move the marker to the chosen action. Afterward, only the latest passed extra-action law can grant an extra action; it is never doubled and does not move the marker. With four vacant offices, Enlist Writer's bonus adds one writer once that turn: if doubled, place three writers total.
answers.evidence: Family action procedure; Enlist Writer row.

answers.answer: After all family actions, if Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one; repeat while both remain. With no Debt, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible, preserving order. The initial queue cost is paid by the family to the bank; seeking a share never pays family cash to Company treasuries.
answers.evidence: Family—Seek Share and New Company shares.

answers.answer: Fill vacancies in ascending number on card backs. For an ordinary hire of your own family, get verbal consent from every other player represented in that office's candidate pool; Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt. On promotion, move the fatigue to the new card and insert the former office card as vacant in ascending hiring order. If no candidate exists or the hirer is vacant, skip the office; it stays vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.

The former Chairman announces how many shares make a pure majority (more than half current shares). Any shareholder may campaign; the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. Move one of the winner's shares to the Chairman slot; it remains a Company share for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in a firm. If nobody wins, former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including self. If Court is empty, former Chairman automatically returns, using supply or, if needed, a prize piece and losing that prize's VP; if impossible, there is no Chairman.

First commit the required resources and cash; for a Company-office check, all check cash comes from that acting office's treasury and is paid to the bank. Gather dice, subtract penalties, then roll and use the lowest die: 1–2 success; 3–4 failure, retry if resources and office limits permit; 5–6 catastrophic failure, ending that office's actions, returning its holder to supply, discarding fatigue and flipping its card to Vacant Offices. Specific procedures can modify this. Do not take a dead action with no effect or chance, such as trading with no ship or deploying with no dice just to test officer losses.

The Chairman may add up to three Debt freely, each adding £5 Balance. Each additional advance requires consent of players controlling a majority of Company shares (Chairman counts). Never advance past the Debt track end. Allocate all Balance to other offices' treasuries, reducing Balance by each transfer; borrowing and allocation may be interleaved while observing the limit. Existing office cash remains there for that office.

Shipping must spend its treasury until £2 or less remains. It can lease an extra ship for £2, fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without owner consent, or buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Put each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China once created. Extra ships last only until Refresh.

The President declares regions including its home and only those reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 of that President's treasury buys one die; subtract one die per declared nonhome region. A successful Trade fills up to one order per ship in that Presidency's sea zone: first writer goes to home port, each later order extends this Trade's connected route. Writers from another Presidency cannot extend it; if writers run out, use filled-order tokens for remaining ships, and these tokens continue the route. Do not fill another Presidency's home region. Add each order's printed revenue to Balance, or half rounded down if a firm already filled it this turn; President receives £1 per order and writers' owners £1 per placed writer. Only one successful Trade per President per turn; failed attempts/retries are within its uninterrupted opportunity.

A Commander may target their own Presidency's home, an associated region, or a region bordering an associated region, but not another home or another Presidency's Company region. A Company region must have unrest or a closed order to make the action meaningful. Exhaust officers/regiments for one die each and local alliances for their printed dice; subtract target and all other regions in its empire (count target once), with Company defense strength zero. Roll; noncatastrophic failure may be retried with remaining resources. After every attempt, owners roll one die per officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 returns that officer to supply. Regiments do not incur officer-loss rolls.

On success, loot is £4 per target tower plus faceup loot modifier, with a minimum equal to surviving officers used in this attempt plus one. Distribute each payout cycle: Commander family £1 for Commander plus £1 per own used surviving officer; other families clockwise £1 per used surviving officer; bank last £1 per used regiment and each used alliance piece. Repeat the cycle until loot is gone. Commander gains one trophy per target tower. Then remove target tower and dome (and all matching empire flags if capital), open all target orders and remove unrest; for a new conquest turn control token symbol-up above associated President's box, put Governor overlay on map and only Governor card in Vacant Offices; move Elephant inside if it faced outward. Governor General means no new Governor/overlay. Catastrophe returns half Commander's family trophies rounded up and Commander to supply; exhausted officers still check losses.

Governor rolls the current printed dice pool without penalty on each attempt, then reduces the pool by one regardless of result. On success take £1, or £2 if the immediately preceding roll was unsuccessful, then choose exactly one: one ship-building stage, one regiment in the Army associated with that President, or add an unsplit £2 to Company Balance or that President's treasury. Each Tax after the first this turn adds regional unrest. Any unsuccessful roll adds one unrest; catastrophe also removes officeholder normally. Repeat with shrinking pool until stopping, no dice, or catastrophe. Ship construction takes two successful actions: first places partial ship in Governor's region; next completes it to the associated President's sea zone.

Company reduces Balance by £1 per Debt, each officer/regiment in an Army and each ship in sea zones (including China), excluding Commanders. If short, take £5 emergency loans; each raises Debt only if a track space remains, but at max Debt keep taking loans without further Debt increase. Newly added emergency Debt has no expense this turn; after loans set Balance to zero. One or two loans lower Standing one; three or more lower it two. Then compare remaining Balance to expectations at current Standing; if short, lower Standing one. Chairman may pay affordable dividends at £1 per Company share; if total paid is strictly more than expectations, raise Standing one. Failure at leftmost Standing causes Company failure.

Resolve the primary Elephant Crisis first, then secondary unrest Rebellions in Bombay, Madras, Bengal Army order; within each Presidency its Commander orders associated regions. Primary normal Crisis strength is normal attack strength plus unrest in target; Foreign Invasion primary uses only its ordinary die. Each secondary attack strength is only unrest there. Associated Commander exhausts active pieces equal to attack strength or as many as possible; alliances are usable once and cannot split purposes. If newly exhausted strength equals Crisis strength, attack fails/defense succeeds: remove all attacked-region unrest, Commander gains a trophy, and if a normal primary Invasion remove one attacker tower if possible. If totals differ, attack succeeds/defense fails and Region Loss occurs.

A vote with support 0 or more passes: place law among passed laws, PM takes passed-law token, resolve chosen policy, then immediate law effects. Support −1 or less fails: discard law, resolve dilemma's If Failed text, Opposition Leader returns token and takes PM dial, then moves proposed policy one adjacent space and resolves it. Finally restore all used voting cards. If law causes failure, finish the vote before scoring. Drawing a dilemma forces that dilemma and ends law drawing.

In 1758 and Long 1710, before London Season, PM may call a special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. Use ordinary voting/support threshold except: pass lowers Debt one per two current Debt, sets Standing to S, gives PM passed-law token and activates firms; fail raises Company-share scoring value by flipping/placing Court VP token (maximum ±3). No policy accompanies it; failure does not remove PM or discard Deregulation law, and PM may vote against. 1813 starts deregulated.

To form a firm, you must manage none: return an eligible Company share to supply or flip a workshop to invested side, flip your board to firm charter, place a family member as first firm share, set value to leftmost and take £5 from bank into London. With manager consent, same contribution creates one share and £5 bank-to-London; up to ten shares, further investments still add £5 but no share. No Chairman share; no Company-share investment if Standing or Debt is lined; cannot use shares created this turn even if traded away. Invested workshops stay invested, losing bonus and failure VP even if firm fails.

Each firm gets one trade attempt per turn and must have a ship to select a trade strategy; it may choose a closed home port, but that port must be open when filled. Manager secretly selects strategy and London bid; reveal bids together, keep strategies facedown until matching Presidency. There roll one die per committed £1, pay bid to bank; at least one 1/2 permits trade. Initiative is ship count minus successful dice; after Presidency's successful Trade, lowest initiative fills first, President decides ties (no automatic Company priority). If President vacant or does not successfully trade, firms fill after Commanders/Governors, with Chairman breaking ties. Fill open orders along own connected route from home, up to ships+1; firm cannot refill own earlier order this turn, but may refill another trader's order. Previously filled orders pay half rounded down. Advance Value one per full £6 added to India treasury this turn.

At start of Revenue, firms pay £1 per charter ship plus the higher of share count or firm value, from London and/or India. If unable, dissolve unless rescued: shares to Debtor's Prison (−1 VP each), ships to shipyards, charter flips family-side; workshops remain invested. Rescue by normal emergency investment (even at ten-share cap, still contribute; pay expenses, lose remaining cash, lower Value one per investment) or emergency merger with one other firm, whose expenses must be paid first and which covers the endangered firm's unpaid costs. After expenses, dividends come only from India: each costs £1 per firm share plus £1 manager. Shareholder may waive only with manager consent; track total cash actually paid, not per-share dividend. Sweep remaining India cash into London.

The supply section says components are limited: complete as much as possible when a supply runs out. Cash, trophy/passed-law tokens, dice and regiments may use proxies. Company Balance, VP and Vote tracks are unlimited. All information is public, including discards and family cash, except facedown blackmail and firm strategies/bids temporarily concealed during selection.

Negotiable: enterprises, facedown blackmail, family cash, Company/firm shares and promise cards. Not negotiable: officeholders, writers, officers, prizes, spouses, trophies, passed laws, played blackmail, PM dial or Chairman piece. Transfer a share by returning old owner's family member and replacing it at that share's location with a member from receiving family; adjust VP for luxury ownership. Blackmail must remain facedown when traded; once used faceup it cannot be traded.

Immediate transfers are binding; future-behavior promises are not, except a printed promise card's guaranteed effect may be called if possible and within its timing/limits. If simultaneous calls cannot all be fulfilled, guarantor chooses which to fulfill. Promise cards may transfer to a third party or back to guarantor. A transferred resource cannot activate twice (for example, workshop bonus is not paid again after sale during that same Bonuses phase). No promise calls or negotiations during Final Scoring.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Agreement / promise rule; scoring introduction.

answers.answer: Use the scenario's player setup cards; add three extra cards for five players or six for six players, shuffle/deal evenly, and take listed cash, enterprises and positions. Place holdings according to setup table: offices with member plus matching office card to owner; shares in Court; writers/officers/trainees in indicated boxes; Commander in Army Commander slot without card; ship with shipyard in listed sea zone or on shipyard if unfitted. Each starting luxury gives 2 VP. Shuffle prestige and blackmail together as one deck; deal three to display, prestige faceup and blackmail facedown.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2–4 and holding placement table.

answers.answer: Game ends after scenario's final turn or when Standing reaches failure. If failure happens during Events in India, finish that phase before Final Scoring; if legislation causes failure, finish the vote. Once game over, stop negotiations, promise calls and blackmail unless a card expressly allows final-scoring use. No negotiations or promise calls during Final Scoring.

Power counts enterprises and Company shares at current track rates (bottom two positions zero), +1 each passed-law token and trophy, +2 PM, plus printed card power including blackmail faceup/down and applicable spouse. First/second awards: turns 1–3 = 3/1 VP; 4–6 = 5/2; 7–8 = 8/4. Tied first players each receive only the lower award and no other award; tied second receive none. Highest final VP wins; tie breaks by most windows, then clockwise from PM.

Final scoring: first score firm shares and Debtor's Prison, then eligible firm special retirement, then Power, then Court/workshops, then Company outcome. If Company survived, add Court VP value per share; if failed, subtract it and add 1 VP per uninvested workshop (invested workshops do not score). Survived: roll office attrition, retire Pensioners, no display cards. Failed: draw one random Company failure card instead of final retirement. Firm special retirement still happens before Power in either outcome.
answers.evidence: Final Scoring order; Court/workshops; Final retirements/failure card.

answers.answer: Spouses usually add VP, impose permanent restrictions and cannot be transferred. Take required enterprise/share trades immediately on acquiring spouse. Retirement discounts stack, are personal, and each can be used once per London Season and once during Final Scoring; they reduce actual spending and prestige priority. For firm special retirement, discounts count toward actual cash spent under dividend cap.
answers.evidence: London Season—Spouses and retirement discounts; Special retirement.

answers.answer: If a shipyard is returned because of Violet Effingham or unpaid tax, its fitted ship stays in play. That shipyard cannot be purchased while its matching ship remains in play; it becomes purchasable after the ship returns.

Enlist Writer: place in any Presidency Writers box; with at least four vacant offices place one extra writer once that turn. Enlist Officer: place in Officers-in-Training. Purchase Luxury: £4 to bank, gain luxury, 2 VP while owned, window icon, social enterprise. Purchase Shipyard: £2 to bank, take yard and matching ship unfitted on yard; shipping enterprise, one vote and £1 bonus while fitted. Purchase Workshop: £5 to bank, manufacturing, two votes and £1 bonus; worth 1 VP on Company failure unless invested. Seek Share: place member in an empty Stock Exchange queue space and pay bank £2, £3, £3, £4 or £5 according to space; it is applicant, not yet share.

If no family member is in supply when placing a piece, take one from any of your prizes and lose that prize's printed VP; this also applies to firm-share creation. If no Family action is possible, take none and return opportunity marker to supply.
If Court is empty, the former Chairman automatically returns as Chairman, placing a member from supply or, if needed, a prize (lose that prize's VP). If that is impossible, there is no Chairman.

Chairman hires Director of Trade from current officeholders other than Chairman/Governor, or any writer if all offices vacant; hires Manager of Shipping from any writer; hires Military Affairs from a Presidential Commander, else any officer, else any trainee. Director hires President from a writer of that Presidency or its associated Governor. Associated President hires Governor from a writer or officer in the region (not Commander). Chairman chooses any writer for China Superintendent, hired immediately on creation; Governor General is hired same way and replaces Director. Ordinary own-family hires require consent of every other player in candidate pool; Chairman election and Commander appointments are exempt.

Director can repeat Special Envoy checks, paying £1 from own treasury per die, no penalty. Success either opens one closed order in a non-Company region or opens China by placing Superintendent overlay/card and having Chairman immediately hire a writer. After finishing all envoys, Director may make up to two transfers, each moving one writer or ship between any Presidencies/sea zones (including China once created). Transfers cannot occur while still taking envoys.

Military Affairs may first make up to two transfers of one officer or regiment between Armies, staying in top half; then assign every trainee to any Army's top half. Finally appoint Commanders: if vacancy or a family has more total pieces in that Army than incumbent's family, choose among families with the most pieces; move chosen officer to Commander slot, return prior Commander to top as officer. Tie with incumbent's family does not replace them. Nepotism does not apply.

Each President chooses order of its Commander, Governors and Trade; each position completes all actions before the next, and Commander/Governors may decline. Trade may be before or after them but cannot interrupt one. A vacant President means Chairman sets order only; Chairman cannot Trade or approve local-alliance purchases for that Presidency.

Trade does not exhaust ships. Refresh returns writers to their associated Presidency's Writers box (dividers preserve affiliation); filled tokens and dividers return to supply. Fitted player ships keep fatigue. Extra ships return to supply.
answers.evidence: Presidency operations and Trade; Upkeep and Refresh.

answers.answer: At the start of Commander operations, before Deploy, request President's treasury funds for printed-price local alliances; President must approve. Move purchased alliances to top/active. For Deploy or defense, exhaust the whole alliance to bottom; its strength is usable once and cannot be split among purposes. Refresh exhausts unused active alliances and never reactivates alliances, unlike officers/regiments.

Deploy into an already Company-controlled region to reopen orders or clear unrest has zero Company defense penalty and no remaining tower, so gives zero tower trophies. With no tower or faceup loot modifier, loot equals the minimum: surviving participating officers plus £1 for the Commander, distributed normally.
answers.evidence: Deploying in an already Company-controlled region.

answers.answer: A Governor needs two successful Build actions total: first successful action places a partial ship in Governor's region; a later successful action completes it to the sea zone of associated President. Partial ship has no other effect. Each successful Commission places one regiment in the Army associated with Governor's President; it has officer-like strength, loot is paid to bank, and it has no officer-loss rolls.

China is created by successful Special Envoy or Envoy to China law; in either case Chairman immediately hires any writer. Superintendent treasury holds ships, not cash. Shipping and Director may send ships there as to any sea zone. It acts after Bengal; Governor-General order replaces Director position but China still follows Bengal. China ships count Eastern for expenses, events, storms and laws.

China gets only one Trade attempt, including failed attempt; no retry. Do not attempt without an export icon in Company-controlled regions. Roll one die per ship. On success count export icons only in all Company-controlled regions: Company Balance gets £4 per icon, Superintendent's family gets £1 per icon from bank. Non-Company exports pay neither amount.

When Governor General law takes effect, all Governors become Pensioners; remove overlays and partial ships; return Governor/Director cards to box. Replace Director with Governor General, preserving holder and fatigue, and put ribbon overlay. Later conquests create no Governor/overlay; printed Company symbols show control. Region Loss skips Governor elimination. (The summary does not specify additional transfer of Governors' fatigue beyond the return instructions.)

Before checks, Governor General adds £3 Balance per Company region. Govern can repeat, paying £1 from own treasury per die, no penalty, but at most one successful Govern per turn. Every rolled 6 adds one unrest to each Company region even on success; failure adds another unrest to each Company region. On success, bonus £1 per Company region and choose exactly one benefit per region: complete a Company ship into any sea zone including China, add regiment to any Army, or add £2 to Balance/any office treasury except own and add unrest to a Company region. Multiple Tax choices this turn must place unrest in different regions.

Storms affect player-owned ships in rolled sea zones: roll once per ship; 1–2 nothing, 3–4 fatigue (or sink if already fatigued), 5–6 sink. Sunk ship returns to shipyard unfatigued. Company and extra ships are exempt. China ships count Eastern; firms use their strategy zone, while Hobnob ships are exempt.

When an order closes, return any writer on it to its owner's supply; flip filled token to closed. If an event closes an order in an already fully closed region, Cascade by closing all open orders directly connected to that region's orders; if a connected order is already closed, close that region's northernmost open order instead. If none open, it also Cascades. A region can initiate Cascade only once per event tile but can receive effects of multiple Cascades.

Turmoil closes northernmost open order in the top-stack region; if all closed, Cascade. Windfall pays owners £1 per writer on orders in top-stack region and every bordering region. Shuffle: Elephant's March, shuffle that event into remaining draw stack, and separately shuffle discards and put them on top; if draw stack is empty, March last instead. Events generally use region on back of new top draw-stack tile, not just-drawn tile, unless their rule says otherwise.

Leader: if top-stack region is sovereign, add one tower. If dominated, it instead rebels using printed explosion modifier. March only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that successfully rebelled.

Peace with Elephant on a border: open orders connected across its border and add one tower to each touched non-Company region. If wholly inside a region instead, open all its orders and remove its unrest. Then March in either case.

For a normal non-Company Invasion, compare attacker's whole empire strength plus event modifier against defender's whole empire strength; attack must be strictly greater. Success replaces defender's flag with attacker's dominated flag; taking a capital shatters that empire. If attacker has no empire, use free capital/star flag plus matching small flag; if none available, no new empire/flags form.

For a non-Company Rebellion, compare only rebelling region strength plus modifier to its sovereign capital's strength; other empire regions do not count. Attack must be strictly greater, so a tie fails. On success actor becomes sovereign and removes its flag and closes its orders; on failure remove one tower from the capital.

On Region Loss, Commander returns half family's trophies rounded up and Commander returns to supply. Roll one die per officer in Army; each 6 removes officer. Eliminate Governor: card to unused stack, fatigue and member to supplies. Remove overlay, partial ship and unrest. Restore dome with one tower (or Foreign Invasion-specified strength) and proper flag; return control token with £ loot side down and region-symbol side up. Invasion Crisis closes orders (Cascade if already closed); Rebellion/Foreign Invasion already close them. Standing falls by number of regions lost so far this turn: first −1, second an additional −2, and so on. Loss does not automatically remove any other Company region; resolve each attack/defense separately.

After successful Invasion Crisis, Elephant moves to the successful capital (Imperial Ambitions); otherwise March to top-stack region. Put it fully inside a Company region; in a dominated region point toward sovereign; in sovereign point across shape-marked border on tile. If that neighbor is already dominated by actor, choose first clockwise neighbor not so dominated; if all are, use redirect-arrow border toward empire capital.

Foreign Invasion targets by storm-die roll: West targets Bombay, South Madras, East Bengal, all storms each, none the top-stack region. For each target roll ordinary attack die and resolve Invasion/Company attack. Success closes all target orders (Cascade if already all closed), removes target flag and all matching flags if capital, restores dome if Company-controlled, and sets tower strength to half attack roll rounded down. March with circle shape only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that was invaded. For Company defense, primary strength is the ordinary die, with no unrest added; secondary unrest attacks still apply.
answers.evidence: Events table—Foreign Invasion; FAQ—Foreign Invasion and unrest.

answers.answer: PM must draw at least one law. After one or two ordinary non-dilemma draws, PM may stop or continue up to three total, then choose one revealed law and discard others. Drawing a dilemma forces selecting it immediately and ends drawing. Before voting, move dial arm clockwise or counterclockwise to the first policy space matching chosen law's bottom icon; that space fixes target and consequence.

Tax: each family pays £1 to bank per target owned; unpaid targets return to supply, including Chairman. Window tax additionally charges each window on enterprises and each prize; if unpaid return enterprise/prize member. Bonus: bank pays each family £1 per target they own. Power swaps target's marker with next higher; if target already highest, swap any other pair.

Starting with PM and clockwise, players cast votes by spending £1 family cash per vote plus printed card votes; each card's votes may be used only once during the entire vote, across rounds, and is rotated until resolution. PM may call another full round or stop after each; a round with no votes ends voting.

A player who voted for can later oppose; once opposed, cannot support during that vote. Track opposition; biggest opponent gets Opposition Leader, with tied current holder retaining. With recipient consent, votes may be cast for someone already opposed or committing to oppose and count toward that person's opposition total. PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprises opposing, except forced use of “Vote with my enterprises” promise.

Final-turn prizes still pay upkeep. If unable, return prize member and lose its printed VP. On nonfinal Refresh, writers go to associated Presidency Writers box; filled tokens/dividers and extra ships return supply; exhausted officers/regiments reactivate; active alliances exhaust and do not reactivate; fitted player ships retain fatigue. On final turn, perform upkeep but skip Refresh and go to scoring.

Each shareholder may make one additional London Season retirement from supply, regardless of number of firms owned. Actual cash after spouse discounts cannot exceed highest total dividend marker of any firm they own a share in; no retirement from a firm with absent or zero marker. Printed cost can exceed cap if discounts cover it. Otherwise normal retirement, including prestige eligibility; discounts available once per London Season and once at Final Scoring. At start of Final Scoring, score firms, then allow one such retirement before Power or other scoring, whether Company survived or failed; no display cards.

Firm investment £5 comes from bank into London; trade proceeds go into India. London pays fitting costs, bids and expenses; expenses may use London and/or India. Dividends are paid from India only. Remaining India cash sweeps to London after dividends. Family cash cannot move into or out of firm treasuries, and London cash cannot buy new equity shares; creating shares requires Company-share or workshop contribution.

Firms phase occurs after Family (including share creation) and before Hiring. Managers resolve timing conflicts within a firm; PM resolves conflicts between firms. Investments happen without set order until no one wants further action, then managers choose strategies.

A firm may fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 from its London treasury to bank, with yard owner's consent. It may buy a player-owned ship already in Company with owner consent: £3 if unfatigued or £2 if fatigued, paid into Shipping treasury. Firms cannot acquire Company or extra ships. Without the owner's consent it cannot fit/buy the player's ship.

Only a player managing no firm may initiate hostile takeover; managing another firm disqualifies. Get consent of holders of a majority of target shares. Move firm's ships, money and shares to the initiating player's charter, copy both cube positions; former manager returns cubes and flips board to family side.

Managers negotiate merger with every shareholder's consent. Highest-value firm is primary; if tied, players choose among tied firms. Move secondary shares, ships and treasury funds to primary; secondary boards return family-side; shareholders may negotiate share transfers. If primary would exceed ten shares, return excess to their owners' supplies with those owners' consent. Primary keeps its value/dividend track. One binding immediate agreement.
Hobnob has no bid, trade or dividends; it still pays expenses and retains its previous dividend marker for retirement. Its ships are exempt from storms.

Yes. Emergency investment follows ordinary Company-share/workshop contribution rules even when ten-share cap prevents new shares: contribution still pays expenses, any remaining cash is lost, and Value drops one space per emergency investment. Same-turn-share restriction applies: cannot invest Company shares created this turn, even if traded away. Workshops are also eligible contributions under ordinary rules.

Emergency merger is with only one other firm. Normal merger procedure still applies, including every involved shareholder's consent. The other firm must first pay its own expenses if not already paid, then pay the endangered firm's unpaid expenses.

Voluntary dissolution requires consent of every shareholder. Use insolvent-firm dissolution: shares go to Debtor's Prison (each −1 VP), ships return to matching shipyards, charter flips to family side. Workshops remain invested for the rest of game; they do not recover.

At Final Scoring, for each player separately, add VP from all shares across all firms and round that player's combined total down once; deduct 1 VP per own family piece in Debtor's Prison. Firm share values: Value 1 −1; 2 = 0; 3–4 = ½; 5–7 = 1; 8–9 = 1½; 10 = 2 VP per share. This firm scoring is first and applies whether Company ultimately survives or fails; then special retirement occurs before other final scoring.
answers.evidence: Final Scoring order; Firm-track VP per share.

answers.answer: 1710 runs turns 1–5, with no deregulation procedures. 1758 runs 3–7 and can vote in deregulation. 1813 runs 5–8 and starts deregulated. Long 1710 runs 1–8, same initial position as 1710 with deregulation available. Deregulation special vote in 1758/Long 1710 is at turn start before London Season.

1710: Standing £10 expectations, Debt 0, each office treasury £3, Royal Protection, one regiment per Army, no Company ships. 1758: Standing £12 expectations, Debt 3, each treasury £4, Calico Acts, one regiment per Army, one Company ship in East Indian, and Bengal control token in Bengal Presidency.

1813: Standing £10 expectations, Debt 0, each treasury £3; initial laws Military Oversight, Deregulation (Debtor's Prison side), Calico Acts; two regiments per Army and one Company ship per sea zone. Put +2/−2 share-value token in Court, create China, place Bombay/Madras/Bengal control tokens in Presidencies, return Governor General law to box and overlay over Director of Trade. Use Governor General instead of Director, no Governors. Copy map from scenario card; starting player ships/offices come from setup cards.
On turns 1–3 Power awards are 3 VP first and 1 second; turns 4–6 are 5/2; turns 7–8 are 8/4. Tied for first: each tied player gets only the lower award; no other award. Tied second receive none.

Initial Power positions: Social 2; Company shares 1; Shipping and Manufacturing 0. Standing expectations track is £4/6/8/10/12/14/16, with reset S above £10. Deregulation eligibility: Standing £4/6/8 and Debt 5/6/7/8 are lined; Standing £4 and Debt 8 are starred. In 1758/Long 1710, lined permits PM to call; starred requires vote.

No. On successful Foreign Invasion, unrest does not increase primary attack strength or set tower level. Use ordinary attack die both for attack and to set towers to half the die rounded down. It closes all target orders once; if already all closed, Cascade. Region Loss does not close them a second time.

If Mercantile/Diplomatic Connection reduces a check to zero dice, it is failure. Company Fraud is played at start of Revenue: roll one die per your officeholder, reduce Balance by twice highest roll (minimum zero), and receive from bank only the cash actually removed from Balance, not more (e.g. £10 balance and 6 highest pays £10). Public Demands Impeachment returns member to supply and office card to vacancies. Military Oversight's demoted Commander may be reappointed as officer.

Set out board/supplies; shuffle India events; local alliances begin in named Army boxes; Balance £5; place Power tokens as indicated, family VP markers at zero, and loot tokens money-side up in matching regions. Choose scenario and follow its setup card for Standing, Debt, treasuries, laws, regiments, ships and political India map. Turn marker starts on scenario date, and PM dial arm points to matching date; scenario determines last turn.

Each turn: London Season → Family → Firms if deregulated → Hiring → Company Operation → Bonuses → Revenue → Events in India → Parliament Meets → Upkeep and Refresh. Eligible special Deregulation vote occurs at very start before London Season. Skip London Season on the first turn.

Retirements start with Chairman; if vacant, start with former Chairman, then proceed clockwise. Each player may retire each pensioner to a prize, paying printed cost and gaining printed VP; pensioners need not all be retired. Set retirement spending aside until London Season ends to determine display priority, then pay it to bank. Prizes may have upkeep/window taxes. Unused Pensioners return to supply after display step.
The surviving capital loses its starred flag and is no longer an empire whenever an empire loses its last dominated region. This applies regardless of cause, including Rebellion or Company conquest.
Per share: Value 1 = −1 VP; 2 = 0; 3 = ½; 4 = ½; 5 = 1; 6 = 1; 7 = 1; 8 = 1½; 9 = 1½; 10 = 2. Each player's total across all firm shares is rounded down once.

Family actions begin with the Chairman title holder, then proceed clockwise. After all players' Family actions, create new Company shares: while applicants and Debt remain, move rightmost applicant into Court, lowering Debt one each time; then if Debt is gone slide applicants right preserving order.
answers.evidence: Family phase opening; New Company shares.

answers.answer: Company Operation order is Chairman → Director of Trade (or Governor General) → Manager of Shipping → Military Affairs → Bombay → Madras → Bengal → China Superintendent if created. Skip vacant offices; a vacant office stays in sequence but takes no actions. Governor General occupies Director position; China acts after Bengal.

Events begin by rolling storm die; resolve all indicated storms before drawing any event. Storm checks are once per player-owned ship in affected zones; Company and extra ships exempt. Then flip and resolve one event tile at a time, for the number of India events shown on storm die. For region-based events normally use back of new top tile in draw stack, not the tile just drawn; follow event-specific location rule.

For ordinary Elephant-located Crisis, Elephant's tail identifies attacker/acting region and head identifies defender/target. Sovereign actor (large capital flag or unflagged dome) means Invasion; dominated actor (small flag or no dome) means Rebellion against sovereign. If Elephant lies fully inside Company region, it is Rebellion against Company. The summary notes sovereign regions have dome without flag or capital/star flag; dominated regions have small flag or no dome.
